Conferences · Greece

How to plan a conference in Athens

Build a venue shortlist around the way delegates will move through the city, the meeting rooms and the programme.

A conference in Athens can pair a full day of sessions with a dinner overlooking the city or an evening on the coast. Start with the working day. Once you know when delegates arrive, how the rooms will be used and where people will stay, you can see which parts of the programme fit together.

Choose a base for the working day

A conference hotel puts bedrooms, sessions and catering in one place. A dedicated conference centre is worth comparing if you need more breakout rooms, an exhibition area or a longer production setup. If rooms are spread across hotels, walk the routes to the venue and test coach access before confirming your room blocks.

The Athens Convention & Visitors Bureau venue directory lists meeting spaces, distances and nearby metro stations. Use it to build a shortlist, then ask each venue for the floor plan and a proposal based on your agenda.

  • Athens Convention & Visitors Bureau venue directory

Ask for a layout with your production in it

Send the venue a draft agenda and a room schedule. Include the stage, screens, production desks and space for accessible seating. Ask how many people the room can hold with that setup, where registration will go and whether queues could block the route to the breakout rooms.

Walk the venue from three perspectives during the site visit. Follow a delegate from the entrance to the plenary, a speaker from the green room to the stage, and a supplier from the loading area to the setup. Confirm what can run in parallel and how long changeovers will take.

  • Compare venue layouts in our Greece planning guide

Plan arrivals before setting the opening time

Map the expected flight arrivals, then schedule the opening around the last major arrival window. The airport has public transport options for independent arrivals. For booked transfers, group flights by arrival time and check luggage capacity, the airport meeting point and hotel drop-off access.

Use the arrival day for registration and an informal welcome if flight times are spread out. On the main conference day, allow time between the last session and an off-site dinner for people to get back to their rooms and regroup.

  • Airport transport information from the Athens Convention & Visitors Bureau

Give the evening programme one focal point

A rooftop reception or a dinner on the Athens Riviera can give guests time to talk after a packed agenda. Check the travel time at the hour you’ll actually leave, confirm the accessible route from the drop-off and ask where the group would go if the weather changes.

Send your dates, headcount, room layouts, expected arrival windows and budget range before requesting quotes. Ask venues to break out catering, audiovisual production, extra setup hours and transfers so you can compare costs on the same basis.
